title: CodeScope MCP Preflight
summary: Local-first MCP server serving Tree-sitter AST intelligence and vector retrieval as tool context for AI agents.
problem: Autonomous coding agents make conflicting or hallucinated changes without structured repository context.
solution: A local-first Model Context Protocol (MCP) server combines Tree-sitter parsing and Chroma vector retrieval to ground agent reasoning before code generation.
architecture: Case-study context: Coding agents need repository context before they decide whether to reuse, extend, or create code. The product boundary is local-first intelligence, not an autonomous code-writing platform.
Repository scan: The CLI establishes a deterministic repository view before an agent asks for context. Components: Python, CLI.
Structural analysis: Tree-sitter exposes syntax-aware structure so retrieval can work with code relationships rather than filenames alone. Components: Tree-sitter.
Context retrieval: Embeddings and a local vector store return relevant repository evidence through MCP tool boundaries. Components: sentence-transformers, Chroma, MCP.
The repository README describes deterministic discovery of Python .py and .pyi files with configured exclusions and root .gitignore handling.
Tree-sitter extracts Python syntax and symbols; symbol-aware chunks are bounded to the embedding model token budget.
Local Sentence Transformers embeddings are stored in telemetry-disabled local Chroma; no cloud embedding API is used.
The read-only query layer supports semantic search, exact/partial symbol lookup, similar-code evidence, and index status.
A CLI and local stdio MCP server expose four read-only tools: search_code, find_symbol, find_similar, and list_indexed_files.
Retrieved snippets are bounded source evidence, treated as untrusted content; indexed source is not executed. Reuse/extend/create remains a developer decision.
outcomes: Open-source MCP tooling for structured repository context before agent actions.
Kept the tool local-first to reduce unnecessary source movement.
Made the preflight decision inspectable before any downstream agent action.
The repository README describes an inspect-before-edit workflow and a deterministic email-validator fixture recommending REUSE; the fixture is explicitly small and not a scale benchmark.
